chunks: And with this chain, from Al-Hasan, from Ali (peace be upon them both)
that he was named Al-Hasan on the seventh day, and Al-Husayn was derived from the name Al-Hasan, and he mentioned that there was no difference between them except the period of pregnancy.
ai.seo_question: How were the names Al-Hasan and Al-Husayn related and when was Al-Hasan named?
ai.summary: This narration from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida* highlights the linguistic and spiritual kinship between the two sons of Ali ibn Abi Talib, emphasizing that 'Husayn' is a diminutive or derivative of 'Hasan,' signifying their shared essence. The note that the interval between their births was only the duration of a pregnancy underscores their close chronological proximity, a detail often cited in Shia scholarship to illustrate the unity of the Ahl al-Bayt lineage. This etymological connection reinforces the theological concept of their complementary roles within the Imamate.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 31-145 According to the same documentation, on the authority of Al-Hassan ibn Ali (a.s.), on the authority of Ali (a.s.),
“They named my son Al-Hassan on the seventh day (after his birth). Al-Husayn’s name was derived from Al-Hassan. There was not any more than one period of pregnancy difference between their birth.”
